## per-player-spell-ordinal

Blocks **5** cards.

- **(trigger_event)** A **per-player, filterable ordinal on the SPELL_CAST event**, so a `spell_cast` trigger can ask at queue time "this was that player's Nth spell of the given kind this turn" -- exactly what `data["nth"]` already is on the DRAW event, and answered the same way: the ledger tally is bumped in `state` on the SPELL_CAST fold, so write the post-bump ordinal onto the event as it is emitted and let `triggers._matches` compare it against `TriggerSpec.nth`. The ordinal must be countable over a **subset** of the caster's spells, because the printed clause is 'their first *noncreature* spell', not their first spell: a player who casts a creature and then an artifact is casting their first noncreature spell with the artifact. So either the event carries a small set of per-kind ordinals, or `nth` on a `spell_cast` trigger is scored against the trigger's own `filter` (the ledger already keeps `spells_cast_ids` per player, which is enough to count the filtered run). This turns on the whole 'a player casts their Nth <kind> spell each turn' family at once -- Esper Sentinel, Ledger Shredder ('Whenever a player casts their second spell each turn'), and every 'whenever an opponent casts their first spell each turn' tax -- rather than this one card. Nothing else about Esper Sentinel is blocked: the taxing half is the shipped Mystic Remora shape (`may` with `pay` and `player: {"controller_of": "subject"}`, `else: [draw]`), and the variable price is `pay: {"mana": "{1}", "times": {"power_of": {"self": true}}}` -- `CostModel.times` is documented as read by `may`'s `pay` and is applied as `cost.mana.scaled(...)` in `effects/ops_control.py`, so the {X} clause needs nothing new.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Three near misses, each verified in source. (1) `TriggerSpec.max_per_turn` is the one the packet notes nominate for 'first ... each turn', and it is correct only when the caster is the ability's controller ('whenever **you** cast your first instant or sorcery spell each turn', the single shipped precedent). `triggers._queue` counts it under `key = (obj.oid, ability.index)` -- one cap for the permanent, per the carddef comment 'counted per permanent' -- and Esper Sentinel's clause is scoped per **opponent**: 'an opponent casts *their* first'. In a pod, opponent A's first noncreature spell would consume the cap and opponent B's would trigger nothing, so the card silently taxes one seat per turn instead of every seat. This engine is multiplayer by construction (`GameState.num_players`, `PLURAL_PLAYER_SPEC_NAMES` documenting 'a pod makes it three of them'), so this is a wrong card in ordinary play, not at an edge. The shipped `controller: "opponent"` + `max_per_turn: 1` precedent is not this shape -- its printed line is literally 'This ability triggers only once each turn.' (2) `TriggerSpec.nth` asks the right question but has nothing to read: `EventType.DRAW` is the only event that carries `data["nth"]`, written by `draw_cards`, and `triggers._matches` compares `event.data.get("nth")` against the spec -- a `spell_cast` event carries no ordinal, so `nth: 1` on this trigger matches None and the ability never fires. (3) The trigger `condition` form -- `cmp` over `{"spells_cast_this_turn": {"player": {...}, "filter": {"not_types": ["Creature"]}}}` against 1, which the per-player filtered tally in `values.py` really can compute -- is the near miss this codebase already documents at length as wrong, and for a reason that bites Esper Sentinel in its commonest line: intervening-ifs are re-checked on resolution (603.4, `stack.resolve_top`), and the tally moves in between. The opponent casts a noncreature spell, the trigger queues with the tally at 1, they hold priority and cast a second noncreature spell in response; the tally is now 2, so the first trigger's re-check reads 2 and resolves `skipped="condition"`, and the second trigger's does too. The card draws nothing where it should draw once. Loosening the comparison to `<=` trades that for firing on every spell after the first, which is Rhystic Study rather than Esper Sentinel. Only a queue-time predicate on the event is both, which is precisely what `nth` is and precisely what SPELL_CAST does not carry.
- **(trigger_event)** A **per-player ordinal on the SPELL_CAST event**, read at queue time, so a `spell_cast` trigger can say "this was that player's Nth spell this turn" -- exactly what `data["nth"]` already is on the DRAW event. The tally is already kept: `GameState._tally` bumps `ledger.spells_cast[pid]` on the SPELL_CAST fold, and `emit` runs that fold *before* the caller hands the event to the trigger bus, so the post-bump ordinal can simply be written onto the event as it is emitted. `triggers._matches` would then compare `event.data.get("nth")` against `TriggerSpec.nth` the way it does for a draw, and `loader.__init__` (currently `if model.trigger.nth is not None and model.trigger.event != "draw": raise`) would widen to allow `nth` on `spell_cast`. Mangara needs only the unfiltered ordinal (`nth: 2`, any spell); Esper Sentinel in the same family needs the ordinal counted over a **filtered** run ("their first *noncreature* spell"), which `ledger.spells_cast_ids` already records enough to compute -- so scoring `nth` against the trigger's own `filter` closes both at once. This is the whole "a player casts their Nth spell each turn" family: Mangara, the Diplomat, Ledger Shredder, Esper Sentinel, Mystic Remora's cousins and every "whenever an opponent casts their first spell each turn" tax.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Three near misses, each checked in source. (1) `trigger.nth` asks precisely this question and is refused at load: `src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py` raises "'nth' only means anything on a draw trigger" for any other event, and even if it loaded, a SPELL_CAST event carries no `nth` key for `_matches` to compare, so the ability would match nothing, silently and for ever. (2) `trigger.max_per_turn` is the packet notes' suggestion for a printed rate limit, but it can only say "first", never "second" -- and it is counted per permanent (`triggers._queue` keys the cap by `(obj.oid, ability.index)`), while the printed clause is scoped per opponent ("an opponent casts *their* second"). At a pod, opponent A's second spell would consume the cap and opponent B's would trigger nothing. (3) The trigger `condition` form -- `{"cmp": "==", "left": {"spells_cast_this_turn": {"binding": "event_player"}}, "right": {"const": 2}}`, which really does compute the right number at queue time -- is the near miss this codebase already documents as wrong, in `carddef.TriggerSpec.nth` and in the `esper_sentinel` gap: intervening-ifs are re-checked on resolution (603.4, `stack.resolve_top`), and the tally moves in between. The opponent casts their second spell, the trigger queues with the tally at 2, they hold priority and cast a third in response; the re-check reads 3, the ability resolves `skipped="condition"`, and Mangara draws nothing where he should draw once. Loosening to `>=` (with or without `max_per_turn: 1`) survives the re-check but then fires on the opponent's third and fourth spells, or fires for a Mangara that entered *after* two spells were already cast -- Rhystic Study rather than Mangara. Only a queue-time predicate on the event is both, which is what `nth` is and what SPELL_CAST does not carry.
- **(trigger_event)** A per-player ordinal on the SPELL_CAST event, so a `spell_cast` trigger can ask at queue time "that was that player's Nth spell this turn" -- exactly what `data["nth"]` already is on DRAW, and answerable the same way. `state._fold` already bumps `ledger.spells_cast[pid]` on every SPELL_CAST (src/automtg/engine/state.py:681-687), so the work is: compute the post-bump ordinal where the event is emitted (`game.py:672`, `triggers.fire(state, EventType.SPELL_CAST, ..., nth=...)`), and relax the loader guard at src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py:1406 -- `if model.trigger.nth is not None and model.trigger.event != "draw"` -- to admit `spell_cast`. `triggers._matches` needs no change at all: its ordinal test (src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:913) is already written against `event.data.get("nth")` for any event. The ordinal must be per **player**, not per ability controller, because the printed clause is "a player casts *their* second spell" and every seat gets its own count. This one change turns on the whole "whenever a player casts their Nth spell each turn" family at once -- The Council of Four, Ledger Shredder, Vega, and (with the filtered-subset half that Esper Sentinel's record also asks for) every "first noncreature spell each turn" tax.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: Three near misses, each checked in source. (1) `TriggerSpec.nth` asks precisely the right question and has nothing to read: DRAW is the only event that carries an ordinal (written by `primitives.draw_cards`, src/automtg/engine/primitives.py:72-80), and the loader refuses `nth` outright on any other event with "'nth' only means anything on a draw trigger" (src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py:1406-1415), so the card does not even load. The caster casts their second spell, the trigger queues with the tally at 2, they hold priority and cast a third in response; the re-check reads 3 and the ability resolves `skipped="condition"`, so the Knight is never made in one of this card's most ordinary lines. Loosening to `>=` fires on every spell from the second on, which is a strictly better card. Only a queue-time predicate on the event is both right at queue time and stable, and that is what `nth` is.
- **(trigger_event)** a per-player once-each-turn restriction on a trigger -- say `max_per_turn_per_player: 1` on TriggerSpec (src/automtg/cards/schema.py:276, beside the existing `max_per_turn`), counted in `triggers._queue` (src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:1398) under a key of `(obj.oid, ability.index, actor_pid)` instead of `(obj.oid, ability.index)`, where `actor_pid` is the seat the event was about -- the same seat `_actor` already computes for the `controller: "opponent"` check and that `bindings["event_player"]` exposes. With that one key this card is a single `spell_cast` trigger: `{"event": "spell_cast", "controller": "opponent", "filter": {"not_types": ["Creature"]}, "max_per_turn_per_player": 1}`. It is the clause the whole Rhystic/tax family is printed with, and docs/unsupported-cards.md already tracks it under this same slug for Esper Sentinel, whose trigger line is word-for-word identical to this one.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `max_per_turn` is the nearest thing in `trigger_keys` and it is documented as a *per-permanent* cap: `triggers._queue` keys `state.triggers_this_turn` by `(obj.oid, ability.index)` (src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:1398-1404), so `max_per_turn: 1` says "the first noncreature spell **any** opponent casts each turn". In a duel that happens to coincide with the printed card; at a pod -- where a two-mana legendary Commander creature is actually played -- it silently drops the recruit for every opponent after the first. That is an approximation, not the line. The three near substitutes each fail differently and are all already recorded as dead ends: (1) `nth`, the ordinal filter that would say "their first", is refused by the loader on anything but a draw trigger (carddef.py:441 documents it as `draw` only) because only `draw_cards` stamps an ordinal on its event -- `game._cast` fires SPELL_CAST with player/source/oid/sid/card/kicked and no ordinal at all. (2) A trigger `condition` of `{"cmp": [{"spells_cast_this_turn": {"binding": "event_player"}}, ...]}` counts the wrong things twice over: `TurnLedger.spells_cast` is a flat per-player tally of **all** spells with no type filter, so an opponent who casts a creature and then an artifact is already at 2 and never recruits, while the printed card recruits off that artifact; and 603.4 re-asks an intervening-if at resolution, by which point the tally has moved again. - **(trigger_event)** `nth` on a `spell_cast` trigger, scored per caster: "this was that player's Nth spell this turn", answered at queue time the way `data["nth"]` already is on the DRAW event. `state` folds `ledger.spells_cast[pid]` on the SPELL_CAST branch (src/automtg/engine/state.py:681), so the post-bump ordinal can be written onto the event as it is emitted in `game._cast` (src/automtg/engine/game.py:674) and compared in `triggers._matches` against `TriggerSpec.nth`, which already exists and already does exactly this comparison (src/automtg/engine/triggers.py:913). The loader guard at src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py:1406 -- "'nth' only means anything on a draw trigger" -- then widens to accept `spell_cast`. Trouble in Pairs is the unfiltered case (`nth: 2`, `controller: "opponent"`, every spell counts); Esper Sentinel and Ledger Shredder need the same key scored over a filtered run, so one piece of work turns on the whole "a player casts their Nth spell each turn" family. Nothing else in this sentence is blocked: "attacks you with two or more creatures" is a `creatures_attack_player` trigger with `controller: "opponent"`, `defending: "you"` and a `condition` of `{"cmp": [{"count": {"binding": "attackers"}}, ">=", {"const": 2}]}` -- `attackers` is in `EVENT_BINDING_KEYS` and is the subset declared against that defender (src/automtg/engine/combat.py:589) -- and "draws their second card each turn" is `{"event": "draw", "controller": "opponent", "nth": 2}`, whose ordinal `draw_cards` stamps per drawing player (src/automtg/engine/primitives.py:72). Only the third clause has nothing to read.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `nth` is refused outright on any non-draw trigger by the loader, and even if it were accepted the SPELL_CAST event carries player/source/oid/sid/card/kicked and no ordinal, so it would compare against `None` and the ability would never fire. `max_per_turn` is the key the packet notes nominate for a printed rate limit and it is a *per-permanent* cap -- `triggers._queue` keys `state.triggers_this_turn` by `(obj.oid, ability.index)` -- so it cannot express "their second" at all (it caps how many times the ability fires, not which spell fires it) and at a pod it would be shared across every opponent besides. The trigger-`condition` route -- `{"cmp": [{"spells_cast_this_turn": {"binding": "event_player"}}, "==", {"const": 2}]}`, which the per-player tally really can compute and which `select_players` really does accept as a binding -- is the near miss this codebase documents at length as wrong, and it is wrong here in the card's ordinary line: an intervening-if is re-checked on resolution (603.4, `stack.resolve_top`, src/automtg/engine/stack.py:1024), and the opponent who holds priority after their second spell and casts a third takes the tally to 3, so the queued trigger reads 3 and resolves `skipped="condition"` -- Trouble in Pairs draws nothing on exactly the turn a storm-ish opponent makes it matter. Loosening to `>=` fires on every spell from the second onward, which is a different and much stronger card. `carddef.TriggerSpec.nth`'s own docstring (src/automtg/engine/carddef.py:440) makes this argument for the draw case: only a queue-time predicate is both correct at queue time and stable at resolution.

## token-definitions

Blocks **4** cards.

- **(token)** a token id for a 2/2 blue Bird creature token with flying, e.g. `bird_2_2_u_flying`
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `token_ids` is a closed list and its only Bird entry is `bird_1_1_w_flying` (1/1 white Bird with flying) -- wrong size and wrong color, so four of them is a 4-power white board instead of an 8-power blue one, and every card that reads size or color (anthems, devotion, "blue creatures you control", color-based removal and protection) would read it wrong. The nearest blue flier, `illusion_1_1_u_flying`, has the right color but the wrong size and the wrong creature type, which matters to Bird tribal and to `shares_a_type_with`. `create_token` takes only `amount`, `as`, `attacking`, `controller`, `tapped` and `token` -- there is no power/toughness, color, subtype or keyword override -- so the printed token cannot be spelled from the card, and the brief forbids substituting a nearly-right one.
- **(token)** a token definition for the Pilot this card makes, so `create_token` may name it. Printed exactly: "a 1/1 colorless Pilot creature token with \"This token crews Vehicles as though its power were 2 greater.\"" -- suggested id `pilot_1_1_c_crew2`, name "Pilot Token", types ["Creature"], subtypes ["Pilot"], colors [], color_identity [], power 1, toughness 1, is_token true, added to data/cards/tokens.cards.json. The token is NOT a plain vanilla 1/1: it carries one printed quoted ability, verbatim -- "This token crews Vehicles as though its power were 2 greater." -- and defining the token exactly means giving that line a home too. It is a static ability of the token that raises, by 2, the power this creature contributes while paying a `crew` cost, and only while paying one: it is not a `buff`, because the token stays a 1/1 for combat, for `power_of`, and for every other sum on the board. Nothing in `static_effects` says it (the list has `buff`, `set_pt` and `grant_keyword`, all of which change actual power), and the summing lives inside the cost rather than in characteristics -- `_tap_cost_pool` totals derived power to decide whether a `tap_permanents` with `total_power` is payable -- so the capability wanted is a per-creature crew-power bonus that only that sum consults. Crew itself is not the gap: `tap_permanents` with `total_power` ships and is documented as crew (docs/card-dsl.md "Crew -- a tap cost measured in power", docs/keywords.md marks Crew shipped), so Shorikai's own "Crew 8" line needs nothing new.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `create_token` carries only `token`, `amount`, `as`, `attacking`, `controller` and `tapped` -- `token` is an id string naming a card already in the pool, with no inline token body and no size, colour, subtype, keyword or ability override on the op; `reference.token_ids` is a closed list and `loader.validate_token_references` rejects an unknown id at load time, so the card cannot ship ahead of the definition. The pool has no Pilot token of any size, and no colourless 1/1 with an ability of this shape. The nearest bodies are `gnome_1_1_c` (1/1 colourless, but a Gnome, an artifact creature, and with no ability) and `hero_1_1_c` (1/1 colourless Hero, vanilla); substituting either would give the wrong creature type -- a real cost on a card whose whole point is manufacturing crew -- and would silently drop the +2 crew rider, which is the only reason this token is worth more than a Servo.
- **(token)** a token id for a plain 1/1 blue Illusion creature token with NO abilities -- e.g. `illusion_1_1_u`: name "Illusion", oracle_text "1/1 blue Illusion creature token.", types ["Creature"], subtypes ["Illusion"], power 1, toughness 1, colors ["U"], color_identity ["U"], no keywords, is_token true. It is the shipped `illusion_1_1_u_flying` entry in data/cards/tokens.cards.json with the keywords list dropped and the id and oracle_text trimmed to match, so it is a one-line data change. The vanilla blue Illusion is the standard token of the Jace/Illusion shell, so the single id closes a family rather than just this card.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: token_ids is a closed list and its only Illusion is `illusion_1_1_u_flying` -- confirmed against data/cards/tokens.cards.json, where that entry carries "keywords": ["flying"]. Size, colour and creature type are all right; the flying is not, and the brief forbids substituting a nearly-right token. Flying is not cosmetic on a card whose ultimate also makes those Illusions large: an evasive army and a ground-stalled one are different cards, and the printed token has no evasion. `create_token` cannot spell the difference from the card either -- op_options gives it only `token`, `amount`, `as`, `attacking`, `controller` and `tapped`, with no keyword, colour, subtype or power/toughness override. Nor can the token be patched after creation: there is no remove-keyword op in `ops` at all (grant_keyword only adds), `lose_all_abilities` is a static_effect that would have to be permanent and would strip anything the token ever gained as well, and `animate` on a create_token `as` binding stores an until-end-of-turn TempEffect, so whatever it set would fall off at cleanup where the printed token is permanently a flightless 1/1. The next-nearest ids are `fish_1_1_u` (right size and colour, wrong creature type, and these tokens are meant to be Illusions) and `hero_1_1_c` (colourless).
- **(token)** A token id for "a 0/0 colorless Construct artifact creature token with 'This token gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.'" — suggested id `construct_0_0_c_artifact_buff`. Its printed ability, verbatim, is "This token gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.", which is a static `buff` with `self_only` affects and a counted magnitude: {"kind": "static", "text": "This token gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.", "effect": "buff", "affects": {"self_only": true}, "power": {"count": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Artifact"], "zone": "battlefield"}}, "toughness": {"count": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Artifact"], "zone": "battlefield"}}} — the token counts itself, so a lone Construct is 1/1.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `reference.token_ids` is a closed list and holds no Construct at all. The nearest colorless artifact creature token is `gnome_1_1_c` (1/1 colorless Gnome artifact creature), which is the wrong size, the wrong creature type and carries no ability; substituting it would print a different card.

## extra-turn

Blocks **3** cards.

  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `ops` has `extra_combat` and `extra_land_drop` -- both extra *sub-steps inside* the turn already in progress -- but nothing that adds a turn to the turn sequence, and no `value_key`, `condition_key` or `trigger_event` refers to a scheduled turn either. `delayed_trigger` cannot stand in for the second half: its only durations are `this_turn` and `until_it_fires` (`src/automtg/engine/structs.py:666`), so a delayed `end_step` watcher created by this spell fires at the end step of the turn Final Fortune was cast in -- one whole turn early, and exactly the misfire that makes the card read as printed while doing something else. There is no duration, condition or trigger field that says "the extra turn this effect created".
- **(op)** an `extra_turn` op taking the usual player spec -- and it must accept `"gift_recipient"`, not just "you" -- that queues one additional turn for that seat immediately after the current one, taken before the turn order would otherwise advance, and stacking if several resolve. This is the reward half of a gift, so it has to be writable as an ordinary entry in `spell_effects` placed first (702.164b), the way Parting Gust writes `{"op": "create_token", "token": "fish_1_1_u", "tapped": true, "controller": "gift_recipient"}`.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The `gift` card-level cost itself ships and is not what is missing -- `gift` is in `card_level_cost_keys`, and `gift_promised` / `gift_recipient` are in `condition_keys` and the player specs. What is missing is the thing being promised. The `gift` string is only a label: `src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py` checks it is non-empty and that something reads the promise, and nothing anywhere in `src/` grants a turn from it, so the engine delivers no reward on its own -- the card must spell the reward out as an effect. `ops` has `extra_combat` (with `extra_main`) and `extra_land_drop`, but both add sub-steps *inside* the turn already in progress and neither adds a turn to the turn sequence; no `value_key`, `condition_key` or `trigger_event` refers to a scheduled turn either. This is the same missing op already filed for Final Fortune (`data/authoring/gaps/final_fortune.json`), plus the requirement that its player spec reach the gift recipient. Writing `gift: "an extra turn"` and simply omitting the grant would be the worst outcome available here: the residual gate accepts it (`src/automtg/cards/authoring/verify.py:1170` claims a printed line starting "Gift " whenever the noun phrase matches `card.gift`), so the card would load, pass all six gates, offer the promise in the UI, and never hand the opponent the turn it promised.
- **(replacement)** Two halves, and the first is the same missing concept the `extra_turn` op gap already names: the engine has no notion of an extra turn to replace. `turn._begin_next_turn` (src/automtg/engine/turn.py:837) advances `state.active_idx` by `next_alive_index` and increments `state.turn`, with no queue of scheduled turns anywhere -- `state.extra_phases` / `extra_phases_taken` are extra *phases inside* the turn already running, cleared at that very boundary. Once a queue of extra turns exists, this card needs the second half: a player-wide static -- `skip_extra_turn` in `static_effects`, read where a queued extra turn is about to begin, the way `player_skips_draw_step` (src/automtg/engine/player_statics.py:163) is read in the turn walk -- that takes the usual `affects_player` spec (`"opponent"` here) and, instead of beginning that queued turn, discards it. It must be a replacement on *beginning* the turn rather than a filter at scheduling time, because 614/616 apply when the turn would begin: a Time Warp cast while Trouble in Pairs is out and then answered before the extra turn arrives should still lose the turn, and an extra turn queued before the enchantment resolved should still be skipped. It also removes exactly one queued turn, not the opponent's whole schedule, so a player holding two extra turns loses them one at a time.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `static_effects` has `skip_draw_step`, which is the closest shape and is the model for the plumbing, but it suppresses a turn-based *action inside* a turn (504.1) and reaches nothing about the turn sequence. `ops` has `extra_combat` and `extra_land_drop`, both extra sub-steps within the turn in progress, and `skip_untap`, which is a per-permanent flag. Nothing in `static_effects`, `ops`, `trigger_events`, `condition_keys` or `value_keys` refers to a scheduled turn at all, so there is no object, event or predicate for a replacement to attach to -- the sentence cannot be approximated in the wrong direction either, since there is no way to say "an opponent skips their next turn" and doing so would be a strictly different (and far stronger) card: the printed line touches only *extra* turns and is inert against a normal turn sequence.

As docs/card-dsl.md:9110 says outright, statics do not reach a spell on the stack, so this needs new plumbing in the `counter` op, not a new card field.

## cant-cast-spells

Blocks **1** card.

- **(static_effect)** A player-wide static that **withholds cast actions** from a set of players while it is on the battlefield -- a `cant_cast_spells` entry in `STATIC_EFFECTS` / `PLAYER_WIDE_STATIC_EFFECTS`, carrying `affects_player` (here `"opponent"`) plus the usual optional static `condition` (here `{"is_your_turn": true}`, which `static_condition_keys` already spells), and consulted by `legality._priority_actions` in the same place and the same way `split_second_active` is: when the prohibition is live for `pid`, `_cast_actions` is not extended, so the seat is offered only its mana abilities, land drop and other special actions. Ideally the static also takes an optional filter over the spells it stops, because the whole family is printed that way -- Grand Abolisher ("During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells and can't activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, and enchantments they control"), Drannith Magistrate ("Your opponents can't cast spells from anywhere other than their hands"), Teferi, Time Raveler, Deafening Silence ("Each player can't cast more than one noncreature spell each turn"). Voice of Victory itself needs only the unfiltered form scoped to opponents on your turn. Nothing else on this card is blocked -- the Mobilize 2 half is fully expressible today (see `notes`), so no partial answer was written.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The engine has exactly one cast prohibition and it is the wrong shape in all three dimensions. `split_second` (a `card_level_rider_key`, not a static) is read by `legality.split_second_active`, which walks the *stack* looking for a spell whose CardDef sets the flag; it therefore lasts only while that spell is on the stack, applies to **every** player including its own controller, and cannot be scoped to a turn or to a permanent sitting on the battlefield. `epic` is the other casting prohibition and it is the opposite card: it stops *you* casting spells for the rest of the game, is again a card-level rider on the spell that resolved, and has no seat or duration vocabulary. Nothing in `static_effects` reaches casting at all: the closest entries are permissions and prices, not prohibitions -- `cast_from_graveyard`, `cast_from_library_top` and `play_lands_from_library_top` widen where a spell may be cast from, `spell_cost_reduction` and `attack_tax` change what it costs, `spells_cant_be_countered` protects a spell that has already been cast, and `freeze_opponent_lands` is the only opponent-facing lock in the list but it stops lands untapping, which taxes mana rather than forbidding the cast (an opponent with Treasures, rituals or untapped lands from elsewhere casts freely, and one with no mana is stopped by a card that prints nothing about mana). The `cant_*` family in `ops` and `static_effects` -- `cant_attack`, `cant_attack_you`, `cant_block`, `cant_sacrifice`, `cant_attack_player` -- are all combat and sacrifice restrictions on *permanents*; none is a player-wide casting restriction, and `PLAYER_WIDE_STATIC_EFFECTS` (the 13 statics that take `affects_player`) contains no casting entry. `lock_abilities` is an op that silences a chosen permanent's activated abilities and says nothing about spells. Writing the line any other way would be an approximation of a hard lock: a `spell_cast` trigger that counters the spell is not "can't cast" (the opponent still casts it, still pays for it, still fires cast triggers, and a spell with `uncounterable` or a protected controller gets through anyway), and a cost tax is not a prohibition.

## class

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** Class levels: a level number carried by an Enchantment - Class permanent, which enters at level 1 and is raised one step at a time by a printed "<cost>: Level N" ability that may be activated only as a sorcery and only when the permanent is at exactly level N-1 (levels cannot be skipped, and a level already gained cannot be bought again), plus a per-ability level gate so that each printed ability is active only at or above the level it is printed under, and every lower level's ability stays on. Concretely this wants (a) a level tracker on the permanent, (b) an ability form for the level line itself -- something like kind: "level" with level: 2 and a cost from cost_keys, the way kind: "chapter" carries chapter: 2 -- and (c) an optional level: N on any ability of any kind (triggered, static, activated) meaning "active only while this permanent is at level N or greater". With those three, Caretaker's Talent is: the token-draw trigger at level 1 (already expressible: permanent_enters, batched, filter {controller: "you", is_token: true}, max_per_turn: 1, effects draw 1), a level-2 line costing {"mana": "{W}"}, a level-2 triggered ability (see the trigger_event need below) whose effect is copy_permanent over a target token you control, a level-3 line costing {"mana": "{3}{W}"}, and a level: 3 static buff {"effect": "buff", "power": 2, "toughness": 2, "filter": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "is_token": true}}. The effect bodies are all already sayable; only the level scaffolding is missing.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The nearest thing in reference is the Saga machinery -- ability_kinds has "chapter", ability_keys has "chapter", trigger_events has "chapter" -- and it is the wrong shape in every respect that matters. A Saga's chapters advance by themselves, one lore counter each precombat main phase, in a fixed order the player cannot pay to change; they fire once as a triggered ability and are then spent, and the Saga sacrifices itself at the end. Class levels are bought with mana at sorcery speed, only when the player chooses, and once bought they stay switched on for the rest of the game as a permanent characteristic-defining gate on OTHER abilities -- including a static one. A chapter cannot express "this static anthem is on from now on", because a chapter is a trigger, not a state. Nothing else in reference reaches it either: `ops` has no op that raises a level, `cost_keys` has no level cost, `ability_keys` has no level field, `static_condition_keys` has no level test, and `trigger_events` has no level event. The counter emulation is the dead end and was checked in full, so it does not need checking twice: an activated ability with sorcery_speed_only and cost {"mana": "{W}"} whose effect is add_counters of an invented "level" counter on itself, a static whose condition is a cmp on counters_on >= 2, and a counter_placed trigger filtered on that counter, does compile from the listed vocabulary but is not this card. It puts a counter on the permanent that the printed card does not describe as the thing being bought; it cannot enforce ascending order or one-purchase-per-level, because an ability's `condition` gates the ability's effect, not the legality of a repeat activation, so a player could buy level 2 four times and have four "level" counters; the counter_placed trigger fires again when the level-3 counter lands, so "When this Class becomes level 2" would create a second token copy at level 3; and every one of those abilities would have to claim a printed line it does not implement, which is exactly the half-implemented card the residual gate exists to catch. Per the brief, an approximation that quietly behaves differently is worse than nothing, so no partial answer was written.
- **(trigger_event)** a "becomes level N" trigger event -- fires once, at the moment a Class permanent's level rises to exactly N, and never again (not when it later rises past N). It wants to be a trigger with source: "self" and a level: N key alongside `event`, the way `chapter` pairs with a chapter number, so that "When this Class becomes level 2, create a token that's a copy of target token you control" is a triggered ability whose effect is copy_permanent over a card-level target of kind permanent with selector {"controller": "you", "is_token": true}.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: trigger_events has 39 entries and none of them observe a level change. `chapter` is the closest and is Saga-only: it is driven by lore counters placed automatically at precombat main, not by a paid activation, so it cannot be pointed at a level purchase. `counter_placed` is the only event that fires off a permanent gaining something, and it is wrong twice over -- it would need the invented "level" counter from the engine need above to exist at all, and it fires on EVERY such counter, so the level-3 purchase would re-trigger the level-2 ability and make a second token copy. `ability_activated` fires when the level ability is activated rather than when the level is actually gained, which is a different moment (the level ability uses the stack, so the level-2 trigger must wait for it to resolve) and equally cannot tell level 2 from level 3.

- **(op)** an `as` binding on the `draw` op that records the seats which actually drew at least one card -- "each opponent who drew a card this way". Concretely: add `draw` to `RECORDING_OPS` (src/automtg/engine/effects/__init__.py:31) and have `op_draw` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_cards.py:42) write, under the binding name, the list of player ids for which `replacements.draw` returned a non-empty list of drawn oids -- the same list-of-seats shape `may`'s `as` already writes and the `{"binding": ...}` player spec already reads (src/automtg/engine/effects/selectors.py:1065, "a set of seats"). With only that one key the whole card is spelled with existing vocabulary and nothing else is needed:

{"spell_effects": [{"op": "draw", "player": "each_opponent", "amount": {"const": 1}, "as": "drew"}, {"op": "for_each_player", "players": {"binding": "drew"}, "effects": [{"op": "draw", "player": "you", "amount": {"const": 1}}]}]}

-- `for_each_player` over the recorded seats is the count, so no new `value_keys` leaf is required (a `{"count": {"binding": ...}}` over a seat list would be the alternative, and today `count` counts objects, not players). Everything else about the card is ordinary: Sorcery, {2}{W}, white, `spell_effects`, `zone: "graveyard"`, and in the sandbox the expectation would be hand_size 2 / library_size 39 for player 0 and one card off the opponent's 20.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `draw` records nothing. `op_draw` reads only `amount` and `player`, discards what `replacements.draw` returns, and the loader refuses `as` on it outright: `effects._validate` raises "'draw' records no binding, so its 'as' would name one nothing writes and every read of it would be 0" (src/automtg/cards/loader/effects.py:1273), and the recording ops are exactly ['choose_permanents', 'choose_player', 'copy_permanent', 'create_token', 'discard', 'exile', 'gain_control', 'join_forces', 'look_at_top', 'may', 'mill', 'play_exiled', 'reveal', 'roll_dice', 'sacrifice', 'search_library', 'search_zones', 'snapshot'] -- draw is not among them. So there is no way to name the seats that drew, and every near miss is a quietly different card:
- `{"op": "for_each_player", "players": "each_opponent", ...}` for the second half counts opponents at the table rather than opponents who drew, so it pays out for an opponent whose draw was replaced by dredge (`replacements._dredge` returns `replaced` and no card is drawn) and for an opponent with an empty library (`draw_cards` returns fewer oids than asked). Both are reachable positions in this engine, which is exactly why the printed rider exists.
- `{"amount": {"cards_drawn_this_turn": "each_opponent"}}` is a turn-wide tally over the whole table (`values.py:389`) that also counts their draw steps and any other draw this turn, not "this way".
- `may` is the only existing op whose `as` yields a seat list (Snort, "each opponent who discarded their hand this way"), but Cut a Deal's draw is mandatory -- wrapping it in a `may` would hand each opponent the choice of whether to draw, which the card does not print.
- Recording via a `draw` trigger is not available either: the `draw` trigger event fires per card drawn and an ability's trigger cannot feed a binding back into the resolving spell's later effects.

<details><summary>Cards waiting on this</summary>

- **Cut a Deal** (rank 1018) — `cut_a_deal`
  - Each opponent draws a card, then you draw a card for each opponent who drew a card this way.

</details>

## enters-replacement

Blocks **1** card.

- **(replacement)** a card-level replacement of the permanent's own arrival that can (a) offer its controller an optional cost as the entry is being replaced -- here discarding a land card from hand, i.e. the `discard_selector` vocabulary of an activated cost reused as a replacement's price -- and (b) choose the destination zone on the answer: paid, the permanent finishes entering the battlefield; declined, it goes to its owner's graveyard instead and never enters at all, so no `self_enters`/`permanent_enters` trigger anywhere sees it and it is never on the battlefield to be sacrificed or bounced in response. It must apply on every arrival, from any zone (cast, reanimated, blinked), not only when the card is cast
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The four whitelisted replacements (`self_enters`, `self_enters_tapped`, `self_enters_with_counters`, `self_enters_prepared`) all only decorate a permanent that is already arriving -- ReplacementModel's own docstring says so, and `zones` runs them after the object has been added to the battlefield, reading nothing from `modify` but `tapped` and `counters`. None of them can charge a cost, ask the controller anything, or redirect the arrival to another zone, and there is no `graveyard` destination in that code path at all. The card-level cost keys are the wrong layer twice over: `additional_optional` / `additional_cost` are cast costs, so they would not apply to a Mox Diamond returning from the graveyard or blinked, and neither branch matches the printed card -- a mandatory discard would make the artifact uncastable with no land in hand (it is castable, it just dies on the way), and an optional one that goes unpaid would still let it enter. `replace_leaves_battlefield` and `replace_deaths` are the only existing destination-rewriting replacements and both fire on the way *out* of the battlefield, so they cannot see a permanent that must never arrive; `replace_token_creation` rewrites what is created but, as its docstring notes, deliberately handles the no-object-yet case only for tokens. Carrying the line as a `self_enters` triggered ability running `may` + `discard` + `sacrifice` is exactly the approximation the rules forbid: the artifact would really enter, other enters triggers would see it, and it would reach the graveyard from the battlefield rather than never having been there.

## escape

Blocks **1** card.

- **(static_effect)** an additional-cost rider on the `cast_from_graveyard` static -- a Cost charged on top of the granted spell's own mana cost, drawn from `cost_keys`, so this card's static can carry `exile_from_graveyard: {"count": 3, "exclude_self": true}`. It must be priced and paid by `legality.graveyard_cast_permission` / `Game._cast` at the moment the granted spell is cast (the way `chosen_additional` charges a card's own `additional_cost`), and `exclude_self` has to mean the card being escaped, not the permanent granting the permission -- otherwise a three-card graveyard pays for the escape with the escaping card itself.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `cast_from_graveyard` is the only static that lets a card out of a graveyard and it grants the cast at the card's printed cost with no price attached. Its whole rider vocabulary is `enters_tapped`, `arrived_this_turn_from` and `affects_spells`; the one cost field on any permission static is `pay_life_instead`, which belongs to `cast_from_library_top`, swaps mana for life rather than adding to it, and cannot express an exile. The card-level `graveyard_cost` / `flashback` slot *is* escape and does carry `exile_from_graveyard` with `exclude_self` -- but it is a field on the escaping card itself, set at load time, and Underworld Breach hands escape to cards it has never seen. There is no op or static that writes a cost onto another card, and `grant_keyword` knows only the 34 ability keywords, none of which is escape.
- **(static_effect)** an unbounded `cast_from_graveyard` permission -- `static_max_per_turn` made optional (or given an explicit unlimited spelling) for permissions whose price is itself the rate limit, with `legality.graveyard_cast_permission` skipping the `GRAVEYARD_CAST_SLOT` ledger check instead of defaulting `cap` to 1. Underworld Breach prints no cap at all; the three exiled cards per cast are the whole brake.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The loader hard-refuses `cast_from_graveyard` without `static_max_per_turn` (`if not model.static_max_per_turn`), on the stated grounds that a permission with no rate limit is an unbounded engine rather than a printed line -- which is true of Edgar, Master Machinist's "once during each of your turns" and exactly false of this card. Every accepted value is a finite integer, so any number I could write would be a cap this card does not print: the card is a storm/loop enabler and an invented ceiling is the approximation, not a rounding of one.

## exile-target-spell

- **(op)** a way to move a *targeted* spell off the stack into exile without countering it -- either an `exile` op that accepts a `kind: "spell"` target (reading its stack refs, pulling the item out of `state.stack` and exiling the underlying card), or a `to: "exile"` destination on `counter`.   <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_opening_sequence` (src/automtg/engine/game.py:1293) draws STARTING_HAND, runs London mulligans, and goes straight to turn 1; it never looks at what is in anyone's opening hand, so there is no window in which a card in hand can act at all. `active_zones` defaults to `(Zone.BATTLEFIELD,)` (src/automtg/cards/loader.py:2052) and the non-battlefield zones it is used for are graveyard/exile statics and activated abilities offered by `legality._activate_zones` -- both of which run once the game is already under way, so a HAND-zone ability would have no evaluator during setup. No entry in `trigger_events` is a game-start event: the earliest is `upkeep`, which is turn 1's upkeep and therefore after the starting player has already begun, and a trigger uses the stack rather than moving its own source out of hand. No entry in `condition_keys` asks who is on the play: `is_active_player` and `is_your_turn` are questions about the current turn, and both read true on the non-starting player's own turn, so neither can gate on "you're not the starting player". `put_onto_battlefield` can move a card, but it is a resolution op and there is nothing at setup to resolve it.

## search-opponent-chooses

Blocks **1** card.

- **(decision)** a `chooser` on `search_library`/`search_zones` (a player spec, so it can be `{"target": ...}`) naming who picks from among the cards the search turned up -- the search itself is still performed and seen by the library's owner, but a *different*, targeted player makes the selection out of the revealed pool. Gifts Ungiven, Intuition and Plea for Power's kin all hang on it
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_search` (src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_cards.py:208) hardcodes the asker: it iterates `select_players(ctx, spec.get("player", "you"))` and passes that same `pid` into `ask_objects(ctx, prompt, pool, 0, take, pid, "search")`, so the searcher is always the chooser. The selector's `chooser` key exists (selectors.py:850, and it accepts an arbitrary player spec) but a search never routes its selector through `pick_from_pool` -- the selector is only a match test via `_matches_in_zone` -- so writing `chooser` on a search's selector is silently ignored and the caster would pick their own card, which is the entire card. `two_piles` (ops_cards.py:1339) is the only op whose first decision belongs to somebody else, and its splitter is `ctx.opponents()[0]` rather than a target, it reads `library[:amount]` off the top instead of a searched pool, and the *controller* still decides which pile is taken -- the opposite of "target opponent chooses one".

## search-split-destinations

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** a second destination on `search_library`/`search_zones` for the found-but-not-chosen cards (e.g. `destination: "hand"` plus `rest: "graveyard"`), so one search reveals N, a chosen subset goes one place and the remainder another, with the shuffle still happening once at the end
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `_search` resolves one `DESTINATIONS[spec.get("destination", "hand")]` and hands every picked card to `_move_found` (ops_cards.py:323); cards that were revealed and not taken simply stay in the library. `look_at_top` is the only lookup with a remainder key, `rest_to_bottom` (ops_cards.py:418), and it is a boolean hardwired to `_bottom_in_random_order` -- bottom of library, never the graveyard -- besides reading the top N rather than searching. `two_piles` does carry `to`/`other`, but only over the top of the library and only as a pile split. Sequencing two ops instead is an approximation, not the card: `search_library` to the graveyard followed by a `return_from_graveyard` would put all three cards through the graveyard, firing `leaves_graveyard` and inflating `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn` from 2 to 3, and `search_library` to hand followed by a `discard` would emit two `discard` events (madness, discard triggers) for cards the printing never discards.

## spells-cast-per-player

Blocks **1** card.

- **(value)** a value leaf that reports spells cast this turn *per player* rather than summed -- e.g. a `max_spells_cast_of: "each_opponent"`, or a per-player quantifier over a condition -- so "if **an opponent** cast three or more spells this turn" asks whether any single opponent reached three. Wanted by the whole Trap cycle and by storm-watching cards (Mindbreak Trap, Archmage Ascension-style counters, Guttersnipe-adjacent per-seat thresholds).
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `alternative_cost` with `{"mana": "{0}"}` and a `condition` is exactly the right home for this line -- that half is not the blocker. The condition itself is: `spells_cast_this_turn` (src/automtg/engine/effects/values.py:417) resolves its player spec through `select_players` and then **sums** the ledger across every seat it names, so `{"spells_cast_this_turn": "each_opponent"}` is the *total* spells cast by all opponents. At a pod that is a strictly wider card than the printing: three opponents casting one spell each would switch on the free cast, which Mindbreak Trap does not do. The per-player machinery that exists, `max_count_of`/`min_count_of` via `_counts_per_player` (values.py:509), counts *objects* matching a selector one seat at a time and has no reach into the turn ledger's `spells_cast`; `condition_keys`' `any`/`all` combine sibling conditions and do not quantify over players.

## token-attacking-planeswalker

Blocks **1** card.

- **(op)** create_token's `attacking` must be able to name a **planeswalker** as the attack's defender (506.2's third defender kind), with the token's controller choosing between the named seat and a planeswalker that player controls as the token arrives -- i.e. `attacking` accepting an object spec / a choice alongside the player spec it takes today, and the arriving token recorded against the walker exactly as `combat.add_attacker(..., planeswalker=...)` records a declared attacker. The same widening is wanted on `put_onto_battlefield`, which shares the helper, and it turns on every 'attacking that player or a planeswalker they control' card at once (Adeline, Myrel-style mobilize-with-a-choice, Legion Loyalist descendants), not this one card.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: The closest existing thing is `create_token`'s `attacking` **player spec** -- Ainok Strike Leader's `{"binding": "each_player"}` inside a `for_each_player`, which is Adeline's sentence minus its last five words. It is a player-only channel by construction: `effects/board_helpers._attacking_player` runs the spec through `select_players`, returns a single **pid** or None, refuses a spec naming several seats, and every caller (`create_token`, `put_onto_battlefield`) then joins the token to that seat's attack. There is no key on either op, and no other op at all, that aims an attacker at a permanent. Substituting the player half alone is not a rougher card but a narrower one: this repo's own combat code and docs draw 506.2 hard -- 'attacking somebody's planeswalker is not attacking them' (the Ghostly Prison ruling behind `cant_attack_player`'s planeswalker exemption and `cant_attack_you`'s opposite answer) -- so an implementation that can only ever point Adeline's tokens at the seat drops a real choice its controller is entitled to make every combat, on a board where a walker is usually the reason to attack. Declared attackers already reach walkers (`legal_planeswalker_defenders`, `combat.add_attacker(planeswalker=...)`, tests/unit/test_planeswalkers.py), so the rules subsystem exists and only the token-creation path cannot reach it. The card's other two lines are expressible and no partial answer was written: `vigilance` is a printed keyword, and 'Adeline's power is equal to the number of creatures you control' is a `set_pt` static with `power: {"count": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"]}}`, the Cultivator Colossus shape.

## token-doubling

Blocks **1** card.

- **(static_effect)** a count multiplier on `replace_token_creation` -- Doubling Season / Parallel Lives / Anointed Procession: 'if one or more tokens would be created under your control, twice that many of those tokens are created instead'. The multiplied tokens are *those* tokens, whatever they were, so the static needs something like a `token_multiplier: 2` that scales the pending count while keeping the pending id, alongside the existing id-substituting `create_instead`. It must still respect 614.5 (a replacement applies once per event, so a doubler does not re-double its own output) and stay the token controller's replacement, exactly as `_token_creation_plan` already does for the substitution case.
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `replace_token_creation` is the right static but the wrong axis: `create_instead` is a closed list of token ids and each pending token becomes *one of each id in that list*, which is how Academy Manufactor makes one of each and how Divine Visitation preserves N. Doubling an arbitrary token would mean naming the token that was about to be created, and this card names none -- `affects_token` is omitted for 'one or more tokens', and there is no 'the same token again' value for `create_instead`, whose ids are validated against the token pool by `loader.validate_token_references`. `src/automtg/engine/primitives.py:_token_creation_plan` says so in its own docstring: 'There is no count multiplier and no mode flag, because neither card needs one... a third card of a different shape -- a count multiplier such as Doubling Season ... is more engine work rather than a new row in a card file.' Listing a specific id twice in `create_instead` would double only that one token and would silently convert every other token the player makes into it. `create_token`'s `amount` is on the creating effect, not on the replacement, so it cannot see a token creation from another card.

## variant-dependent-targets

Blocks **1** card.

- **(engine)** a way for a card's own target spec to be declared only under a particular cast-time variant, so one printed target word can have two different selectors -- e.g. a `variant` field on a TargetModel/TargetSpec taking a cast-choice name ("gift_promised", "unpromised", "kicked", "unkicked", "overloaded"), parallel to the existing `mode` field, plus target enumeration in `legality._cast_options` that builds a separate tuple set per variant from the specs that variant activates. Into the Flood Maw needs exactly one target either way: `{types: ["Creature"], controller: "opponent"}` when unpromised and `{not_types: ["Land"], controller: "opponent"}` when the gift was promised, with legality, fizzling and the resolution-time `return_to_hand` all reading whichever one was declared
  <br>Why the existing vocabulary won't do: `legality._cast_options` (src/automtg/engine/legality.py:701) computes `tuples = enumerate_target_tuples(state, pid, card.targets, ...)` **once**, before any variant exists, and hands the identical tuple list to every `_cast_variant` call -- unkicked and kicked, unpromised and each gift promisee. So the promise cannot widen or narrow what the spell may point at; `gift_to` only rides along on the Action. `TargetModel`/`TargetSpec` carry no condition of any kind: `selector` clauses (`selector_keys`) are evaluated against one candidate object in isolation and none of them can ask about the cast, and `gift_promised`/`kicked` live in `condition_keys`, which only an `if` op may read at resolution -- far too late, since the target was locked in at 601.2c. The nearest existing thing is `mode`, which does gate a spec on a cast-time choice, but it is the wrong choice and is refused here twice: `loader._compile_targets` accepts `mode` only on a card whose whole effect tree is a single top-level `choose_mode`, and a mode is a free player election, not the gift promise -- writing the two lines as modes would let a player take the wide nonland-permanent bounce without ever promising the Fish. `bestow` is the one variant that does change what a spell points at, but its list is the fixed rules constant `BESTOW_TARGET` (carddef.py), not a per-variant selector a card may write. The workaround of declaring two specs (t1 creature, t2 nonland permanent) and branching with `if {gift_promised: ...}` at resolution is not the card: both specs would have to be legal and locked at cast time, so an unpromised cast would still require and announce a nonland-permanent target and a promised cast would still require a creature -- two target words where the card prints one, changing legality, what opponents can respond to, and when the spell fizzles. `optional: true` on the second spec does not save it either: it makes the extra target the caster's free choice rather than the promise's consequence. The first printed line, "Gift a tapped Fish", is fully expressible (`gift: "a tapped Fish"` plus a `create_token` of `fish_1_1_u`, tapped, `controller: "gift_recipient"`, exactly as parting_gust writes it), so only the second line is blocked and no partial answer was written.
